gary_2026_11_17_exec_dinner_why_isn_t_ai.title: Exec Dinner - Why Isn't AI Helping SaaS Teams Ship Faster?
gary_2026_11_17_exec_dinner_why_isn_t_ai.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_11_17_exec_dinner_why_isn_t_ai.summary: Gary's Guide: A private dinner for PE investors & the SaaS leaders they back. Most PE-backed SaaS companies have already given their product & engineering teams AI tools, & boards expected faster results from the same spend. For most, the roadmap hasn't moved. Operators see the same release cadence as two years ago. Investors see AI spend that hasn't paid off. Same problem, two seats. Rahul Raina will open with what Celestial Systems has learned putting AI-native development into practice with client teams. That includes how his team shortened the cycle from customer request to production release from quarters to weeks, & scaled feature throughput 4x with the same headcount. The conversation will cover: - How a board can tell real progress from AI activity, starting with how fast a customer request reaches production - How to get the whole team working the way your best AI user does, not just the one or two who figured it out on their own - If AI is writing the code, who your builders are, & what product managers, designers & engineers actually do now Every guest leaves with an AI SDLC playbook & a recorded walkthrough of one use case moving through the full development cycle, from requirements to mockup to working code. Who should attend: PE operating partners & investment professionals backing SaaS portfolios, plus CEOs, CTOs, CPOs & heads of engineering at PE-backed SaaS companies.

gary_2026_11_18_mise_en_table_mutual_sup.title: Mise en Table - Mutual Support Gathering For Food Entrepreneurs & Creatives
gary_2026_11_18_mise_en_table_mutual_sup.label: Startup / Business
gary_2026_11_18_mise_en_table_mutual_sup.summary: Gary's Guide: Building a food brand or business is hard. The stakes are real, the learning curve is steep, & there's no clear roadmap - just a long series of tasks & decisions you mostly have to figure out on your own. What if you didn't have to do it alone? Mise en Table is a monthly gathering for the people doing the work to bring great food & dining experiences to life. This is about creating the conditions for people working in food & beverage to set themselves up for success - by sharing resources, asking hard questions, putting everything on the table, & building the kind of mutual support that only comes from a real community of peers. This isn't another networking event. It's a free, working peer group where food entrepreneurs, creatives, & operators come together to share resources, solve real problems, & build the kind of connections that actually move your work forward. No panels. No pitching. Just a room full of people who get it. Who is this for? Food & beverage brand founders, chefs, bakers, restaurant/bar/cafe owners, food writers, photographers, stylists, supper club hosts, hospitality executives, food tech operators - & anyone else building something in the food & beverage space. Seats are limited to create a safe space for sharing & building real connections. Come as you are - ready to put it all out on the table to set yourself & fellow builders up for success. What to Expect Every session has a simple rotating format - a resource swap, a show-and-tell, a live problem-solving session, Q&A with a guest who supports the industry - plus ample time to connect & find your next collaborator. The format for this session will be Giving & Thanks! Since this is our last gathering before Thanksgiving, let's make it festive with a casual potluck lunch. We'll have postcards on hand to write a letter of gratitude to someone who has made a difference in your life this year. Come prepared with one resource to share: a vendor you trust, a tool that's saved you time, a contact you'd vouch for, a template that's been useful. You'll leave with a list of what everyone recommended - & an invite to our resource library where we'll keep a running list of people, tools, & tips recommended by the community. Agenda Mise En Table: Giving & Thanks: Potluck Lunch, Gratitude Letters, Resource Share 12:00 - 12:15: Arrivals + Lunch Table Setup Coffee & tea provided. Bring a bite to share for our potluck lunch. 12:15 - 12:30: Fill Your Plate + Quick Intros Share your name, what you're working on right now, & the dish you brought. 12:30 - 1:30: Resource Share Share your favorite resources & recommendations over lunch. Come prepared with at least one resource to share: a vendor you trust, a tool that's saved you time, a contact you'd vouch for, a template that's been useful 1:30 - 1:50: Gratitude Postcards & Connections We'll have postcards available for writing letters of gratitude. Unstructured time to follow up on resources & intros. 1:50 - 2:00: Closing + Vote for Next Month's Format + Signup for Holiday Market One ask, one offer from anyone who wants to share. Then we vote for next month's format. Interested in participating in our holiday market? Let us know! Make sure you've opted-in to receive email from us - we'll follow up with a recap, resources, & invite to the next gathering. Meet Your Hosts: Letters from the Table Letters from the Table is a project exploring the ways food connects us with people, places, memories, & the present moment. It is a series of love letters & a platform for creating connection through storytelling & intentional gatherings. Our mission is to highlight the stories of people who express themselves through food, & connect creators of emerging food brands with an audience that is deeply interested in their work. Sign up for the newsletter to receive periodic letters, recipes, invitations to gatherings, & atmospheric content. Joni Goldbach Joni, the creator of Letters from the Table, is a fractional Product leader supporting founders, business leaders, & teams in reaching their goals & creating meaningful experiences for their customers. gary_2026_11_18_ai_build_lab_for_founder.summary: Gary's Guide: Take your idea from concept to launch in a series of interactive sessions. Leverage AI tools to build a live product, put it in front of users, & leave with honest feedback, concrete next steps, & the tools to keep going - no coding background required. Who it is for Current NYU students, Alumni, & Faculty People who code & people who don't. Anyone who wants to test an idea quickly & cheaply before committing time & money to it. Key highlights Hands-on from start to finish. Every session ends with something real in hand, not just notes. Real customers, not guesses. Founders talk to 5 to 10 potential users & put a working product in front of them. Two tracks. No-code founders build with tools like Lovable, Replit, v0 & Bolt. Founders who code use Claude Code or Cursor. Honest checks built in. Founders open & verify every source, set their success target before the results come in, & have a second tool test every build. A live product with a real ask. Each product goes live with a waitlist, pre-order or booking option. Demo day. The series ends with founders presenting to guest founders & investors. Tools they keep. Every founder leaves with the full Leverage kit & their own working setup. What founders walk away with A tested idea. Assumptions checked against real conversations & real data. A live product MVP. Reviewed, tested, & in front of first users, or a clear & cheap "no." A decision & a plan. Continue, change, or stop, backed by evidence, with the next 14-day test written out. Their own working toolkit. Research, idea testing, building & review tools, set up & ready to use. The Leverage kit. Every prompt & tool used in the series. Good habits. Check the sources. Set the target first. Never let the builder grade its own work. A cohort. A group of founders who built alongside them. Session 2: Build Move from validation to a working product. Founders write a focused one-page plan based on customer interviews, building exclusively to test their biggest assumption. An AI verification tool tests the build against the plan before launch, followed by rapid 60-second live demos & peer critiques. PARTICIPANTS LEAVE WITH A live product at a link A real ask on it: waitlist, pre-order or booking A build reviewed & tested independently BETWEEN SESSIONS Founders share the link with everyone they interviewed & post it where their users gather. They track visits, signups, return use & payments.
